zone_verdicts.reasoning: The levels hold; the label 'ordinary bad reaction' is true only for the two-day earnings window. There, $148-149 is the 1-SD level (8.8-9.3%; the '+/-7%' is the expected absolute move, a different statistic), and across the 24 scheduled reports since Nov 2020 (EDGAR Item 2.02 dates against the price file) the worst next-day close was -8.5%, so a Wednesday close below $148.80 would be the worst in that record. On the 1-3 month horizon of the zone's other anchors it is the central case for the low. Half of the 32 analogs closed at least 8.6% under their day-5 close within 60 sessions, and the analog median (-8.4%) matches those stocks' random-day baseline (-7.9%). In NVDA's own comparable windows since 1999 (25-40% drawdown, 20-day vol at least 50%; 445 days, roughly 18 independent windows) a close below the $148.80-equivalent occurred within 24 sessions in 58% (48% without the vol filter). Chip peers giving back last week's median +10% bounce, with NVDA tracking 1:1, is $148. If the analog clock starts at the resignation (11-12 as day 1) instead of 11-09, the median 60-session low is -16.3% ($136), below this zone. Two anchors should be dropped: China-HQ loss at $148-153 contradicts claim (iii), since from the 11-06 base the fundamentals table puts it at $169-174, already exceeded; and put open interest at $150 is positioning, not support.

The range is a fair one-in-four outcome by mid-January on a closing basis, but the stated triggers are wrong. Support for the range: risk-neutral P(close below $140) is 20% by Dec 18 and 24% by Jan 15; 16% of analogs ended 60 sessions below the $130-equivalent and 25% traded there; NVDA's comparable windows closed below it after 42 sessions in 20-28%. Trigger 1 is stale: 17.0x times $7.91 = $134 uses an EPS base that changes Tuesday. An in-line Q3 (2.49 replacing 1.30) lifts TTM non-GAAP EPS to 8.20 and GAAP to about 9.10 before equity marks, so the record-low multiple sits at $139-154, mostly in Zone 1. NTM EPS rolls up 8-16% (my inference: 12.10 = 2.49 + 2.74 + first-half FY28 of 6.87), which puts $162.85 at 11.6-12.5x, already at Broadcom's 2022 trough of 11.74x, and moves the $142 marker to $153-165. Trigger 2 double-counts: since 11-06 NVDA has lagged QQQ by 15.8% and the median chip peer by 20.7%, a revenue-equivalent discount of 14-18%, about the size of the 16% customer; supply constraints and ODM 'direct customers' shrink the true loss further. What plausibly lands the stock here is a weak or withheld Q4 guide (10% under consensus is about $144 in the fundamentals table), gross-margin slippage (71.1% gives $153; ten points gives $139), export licensing on the intermediary channel, a pull-back in Nvidia's customer financing, or the sector leg resuming. The odds shown are for the bottom edge ($130), not for entering the zone.

The zone sits beside tail odds (1.6%, 3.2%, 11.4% for a close below $100), but its own anchors are median outcomes over 12 months. The analog median 12-month low is $123: 56% of analogs closed at least 20% under day-5 within 250 sessions and 25% at least 39% under. NVDA's bad-quartile 250-session fall from any day is -28.9% ($116). Ten of NVDA's 13 past drawdowns of 25% or more went beyond -31.9%, with a median further fall of 33.9% ($108). Risk-neutral odds of closing below the top edge are about 25% by June 2027 (below $120 21.4%, below $130 27.8%), and trading there at some point is likelier still. No 20-35% estimate cut is needed: the Qualcomm-trough multiple on unchanged consensus ($115), record-low P/E on non-GAAP EPS ($119) and a 5% FCF yield ($105) are multiple-only anchors, and 10 of 32 analog lows fell on market-wide lows. NVDA lost 22% in the Oct 6 to Nov 6 sector leg alone, and its beta is 2.25. The stated mechanism also overstates on its own terms: cutting estimates 20-35% while holding a trough multiple double-counts, since the price already equals a 35% cut to NTM consensus at the prior minimum forward multiple of 20.8x. Where analogs ended was better than where they bottomed: median +7.0% against day-5 after 250 sessions, 28% below the $130-equivalent, 6% below the $100-equivalent. Net: a likely place for a 12-month low, an unlikely place to stay.

The defining arithmetic (17.5x times halved EPS = $81) multiplies a trough multiple by trough earnings, which contradicts the precedent it cites. The 17.0x record low was itself the price of the 2018-19 halving: 3.177 / 0.09775 is 32.5x the eventual trough EPS, and the 2022 low was 66x. On halved EPS of 4.64, 32.5x is $151; today's price is already 39x the EPS left after a 2018-sized fall, and $134 reproduces the 2018 precedent in full. 'Fiscal 2019-20' EPS fell 31.8%, not half; the 47.8% is TTM peak to trough. The 6% FCF yield uses TTM FCF at 66% of net income (36% in Q2). The April 2025 low is a chart level set at 32x earnings. A 2022-sized percentage drawdown from a 20.6x start implies about 10x trailing, which NVDA has never had. Only 3% of analogs ended 250 sessions below the $80-equivalent; 16% traded there, all cases I recall as fraud, leverage or market-crash episodes (Valeant, SMCI, UAA, MSFT 2000, BABA), against 10% risk-neutral by Dec 2027. Keep it as a 1-in-20 tail (risk-neutral 5.3% by June 2027) but tie it to the right trigger: an AI-capex bust judged structural. In that case the unmodelled $279B of supply commitments, $108.5B of guarantees and $99B of equity stakes add charges ($0.96 a share per 10% of commitments; $3.40 for a full equity write-off), and the range is not a lower bound: the risk-neutral 5% tail is $78 by June 2027 and $36 by Jan 2029.

logic_errors: Double counting at constant multiple: revenue-loss scenarios are applied to $162.85 at today's 13.5x and 20.6x, but the forward multiple has already fallen about 32% on unchanged estimates. Claim (iii) says the loss of all China revenue is more than priced, yet Zone 1 still lists that loss ($148-153) as further downside. From the 11-06 base the fundamentals table gives $169 for China and $153 for the largest customer.

The attribution behind claim (iii) is unresolved and used both ways. If the 12.7% leg is a governance discount on the multiple, revenue losses are additive and the zones stand. If it is a revenue haircut, Zones 1-2's fundamental anchors are already in the price. The draft asserts the second in its claims and the first in its zones.

Trough multiple times trough earnings (Zones 3 and 4) contradicts the precedent cited. In 2018 and 2022 the price low came at 32.5x and 66x the eventual trough EPS. The 17.0x record low is the same event as the earnings halving, not an independent second factor.

Claim (i) is not supported and conflicts with the draft's own table. At 20.6x the trailing multiple is 21% above the record low, and that gap is Zone 2. Excluding $1.05 of equity gains it is 23.7x, 40% above. Peer trailing troughs have a median of 11.8x (-43%); the peer forward-trough median of 11.2x is 17% below and Qualcomm's 9.5x is 29% below. Six of the draft's Zone 2-3 anchors ($142, $134, $131.5, $119, $115, $105) are multiple-only moves with earnings held.

Multiple and estimates are treated as independent axes when the low forward multiple (10.4x FY28) is the market's haircut to a consensus it does not believe. When estimates are cut, the multiple on the new numbers normally rises, so 'cut the estimate and keep the multiple' overstates.

Horizons are mixed inside each zone. Zone 1 combines a two-day option move, 60-session analog lows, a horizonless fundamental scenario and an intraday print that has already happened. Zone 3 pairs 12-month analog lows, which are median outcomes, with option odds for five weeks to seven months. 'Ordinary bad reaction' is right for Wednesday and wrong for three months.

The odds quoted do not measure what the zones describe. They are risk-neutral probabilities of closing below one level on expiry day, taken at the bottom edge of Zones 2-4 ($130, $100, $80) and mid-zone for Zone 1. Entering a zone is likelier (below $140: 20% by Dec 18, 24% by Jan 15; below $120: 21% by June 2027), and trading there at some point is roughly 1.5-2 times likelier again.

Floors are presented as support. Put open interest at $150 has unknown direction, and dealer hedging can add selling through it. The two-year volume shelf, the 200-week average ($123.60), the April 2025 low and the $148.80 print are chart markers. The record-low P/E is a single 2018 observation, and the forward P/E has already gone 35% through its own prior minimum, which shows own-history minima do not bind.

'Heaviest two-year volume shelf $130-145' is wrong as stated. That band holds 16.5% of two-year volume, while $175-190 holds 26.7%; $130-145 is only the heaviest band below the price. Some 57.7% of two-year volume traded above $162.85, so most recent buyers are under water, which is overhead supply rather than support.

Stale inputs are presented as levels. 17.0x times $7.91 and the NTM-based markers use EPS that changes on 11-17, and GAAP EPS of $7.91 is used for the $134 anchor even though claim (iv) says $1.05 of it can reverse. The same record-low multiple appears in Zone 2 on GAAP EPS ($134) and in Zone 3 on non-GAAP EPS ($119), a difference of accounting definition rather than of events.

The analog evidence is over-read. The 60-session median (-8.4%) equals the random-day baseline (-7.9%), so it carries no event information. It depends on dating the event to 11-09: from the resignation the median is -16.3%. The 12-month lows include unrelated market crashes.
'+/-7%' and '1-SD about $148-149' are two different statistics shown as one. The first is the expected absolute move (7.0-7.4%); the second is one standard deviation (8.8-9.3%).

Claim (ii) is right about cash but too narrow. The 10-Q's own risk language makes licence denials and conditions, not fines, the penalty that matters, and those hit revenue. Claim (iv) lists demand risks as if independent of the scandal, when Nvidia's customer financing links them.
Zone 4's 'earnings halve as in fiscal 2019-20' misstates the record. Fiscal-year EPS fell 31.8% (FY2019 to FY2020); the 47.8% is TTM peak to trough, Oct 2018 to Oct 2019.

The 'clusters' are not four independent confirmations. All lenses share the same price and EPS inputs; $134 appears as both the record-low multiple and the largest-customer loss by arithmetic coincidence; and option levels near $148-150 sit there because strikes and hedging gathered around Thursday's low.
missing_from_analysis: A scenario tree for Tuesday night. In line with unchanged consensus, the valuation levels shift up 8-17%. A Q4 guide 10% under consensus is about $144. Withheld guidance, a late 10-Q, a new legal accrual or subpoena disclosure, a GAAP miss from equity marks, or a paused buyback each need their own branch.

Nvidia's role as financier of its customers, and what happens to demand if the interim chief or the board curtails it. Relevant sizes: $42.4B of equity purchases and a $24.6B receivables build in H1, $36B of capacity backstops, $108.5B of guarantees, $25B of equity commitments.

The commitment schedule against liquidity. $120B of total commitments fall due by January 2027 ($92B of it supply) against $56.6B of cash and debt securities, and Q2 buybacks plus dividends ($25.7B) already exceeded free cash flow ($21.3B).

A sector and market scenario. NVDA fell 22% in the Oct 6 to Nov 6 AI-capex leg before any company news, peers have just bounced a median 10%, beta is 2.25 and the 10-year yield is 5.10%. None of the four zones names this driver.
Share loss to AMD, Broadcom and Google TPUs as a mechanism separate from industry demand; rivals rose 5-19% in the week NVDA fell 12.7%.
Gross-margin sensitivity. All scenarios hold 75.0% although Q3 is guided to 74.0% and each point is 1.5% of FY28 EPS.
Touch probabilities and real-world cross-checks. NVDA's comparable windows and the analogs' end-of-window outcomes were available on disk and were not used to calibrate the option odds.
The intermediary and third-country revenue pool (18-22% of revenue on the old Singapore billing basis; Taiwan-HQ 28%) as the exposure to KYC or licence rules, rather than the 8.2% China-HQ line.

Positioning. Retail and leveraged-ETF dip buying, 1.2% short interest and 43 of 53 buy ratings point to no capitulation. Leveraged-ETF assets, index weights and any forced-selling thresholds could not be sourced from the reachable hosts and remain unquantified.

Recovery paths, for symmetry. The median analog ended above its day-5 close after both 60 and 250 sessions and 22 of 32 regained the pre-event close within a year. Headlines also point to a fast CEO appointment (Tom's Hardware 2026-11-13: board reportedly approached Arm's CEO) and pressure to reinstate the founder (TechCrunch 2026-11-14 petition).

The post-July balance sheet, Q3 buybacks, the size and class period of the securities class actions, and any official confirmation that the company itself is under investigation. None was available; all headline evidence here is headline text only, unverified.

My red-team calculations are reproducible from scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Temp/dbacb4e2-62a8-5da8-88f5-6a2f24aae003/scratchpad/redteam/ (px1.py, emp.py, an.py, an2.py, earn.py, calc2.py). The NTM roll-forward rests on an inferred construction of the stockanalysis forward EPS, and NVDA's comparable-window statistics rest on roughly 10-35 independent episodes dominated by 2000-02, 2008, 2018 and 2022.
red.most_defensible_answer: There is no floor, and the four zones read better as a probability ladder over different horizons than as four separate triggers. $146-153 is the base case for the low, not a bad reaction: it is one standard deviation of Tuesday's implied earnings move, it traded on Nov 12, half the 32 analogs and about half of NVDA's own comparable past windows closed that far down within one to three months, and chip peers giving back last week's 10% bounce would be enough. $129-142 is roughly a one-in-four outcome by mid-January on a closing basis; the likeliest causes are a weak or withheld January-quarter guide, tighter export licensing, or a pull-back in Nvidia's own customer financing, not "the multiple reaching its record low", because an in-line report lifts trailing EPS to about $8.20-9.10 and moves that marker up to roughly $139-154. $98-125 is a tail over weeks (about 3% risk-neutral for a close below $100 by mid-January) but close to the median 12-month low in the analog set ($123) and in NVDA's own past drawdowns ($108-115). It needs either the still-rising consensus to be cut by a fifth or more or the AI-capex sell-off to resume, and the draft's constant-multiple arithmetic overstates it because the forward multiple has already fallen about 32% on unchanged estimates. $65-90 requires earnings to halve and the market to judge the decline structural: at the 2018 and 2022 lows NVDA traded at 32.5x and 66x trough earnings, which on halved EPS is about $150 or more, so this is roughly a 5%-by-mid-2027 tail tied to an AI spending bust, in which $279B of supply commitments, $108.5B of guarantees and $99B of equity stakes would add charges nobody modelled. The option odds quoted are for closing below a level on expiry day; the chance of trading there at some point is roughly 1.5-2 times higher, and NVDA's own history gives no sign the near-dated odds are inflated.

audit.overall:
I ran 35 checks against re-pulled raw sources: 29 confirmed, 5 minor differences, 1 wrong. The one substantive error is the 'record low' label on the 17.0x trailing P/E, which the draft uses in Zone 2, Zone 3 and supporting claim (i).

- **Record-low P/E (wrong):** 17.0x on 2018-12-24 is only the low of the 10-year price file. On the same method, NVDA traded below it on 424 sessions in 2011-13, bottoming at 12.5x on 2011-12-19. A true record-low multiple on today's EPS gives about $99 (GAAP) or $88 (non-GAAP), not $134 or $119.
- **Options:** every figure reproduces within 2 points from a fresh Nasdaq chain pull. The largest put open interest is at $150 (636,808 contracts).
- **Filings:** every 10-Q figure matches, as does the 8-K. The 8-K gives no reason for the resignation and mentions no investigation.
- **Valuation:** the 2018 P/E, free-cash-flow yields, Broadcom and Qualcomm trough multiples, and implied forward EPS all reproduce.
